Implementation Plan

Clarify will hold the issue on a `reason=label_missing` refusal instead of failing. The heal pipeline then stops re-filing it, routing still never falls back to the default branch, and nothing else in the job runs. The swap of `ai:check-triage` for `ai:orchestrator-managed` probably comes from stall recovery's close-and-reissue in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. That script is outside this issue's scope, so it goes to a follow-up issue.

**Implementation plan for #7516: hold, don't fail, when clarify's integration-ref resolver refuses with `reason=label_missing`**

Planning ref: `a0d3499b1feb5904a8112740f359f7ed5a1a57a6` on `main` (Integration branch mismatch: false).

**Answers applied:** Q1 = A (hold the issue, routing still refused), Q2 = A (make the `always()` steps tolerate a job that stopped before setup), Q3 = A (record the creator script and file a separate follow-up issue).

## Automation and wiring
- This only changes existing code: `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`. No new script is added. Nothing new needs wiring, since the hold runs inside the existing clarify job. That job starts from `issues: opened` and `issue_comment` through `internal-clarify.yml` / `ai-clarify.yml`.
- `internal-clarify.yml` only calls `clarify.yml@main`, so it needs no change. The fix takes effect when it merges to `main`.
- No long-running supervisor, no database work, and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the `resolver_pr_not_open` handling in clarify.yml's `refctx` step, the per-step `if:` gate pattern clarify.yml already uses for `env.CLAUDE_CAPACITY_WAIT`, and the `_run_refctx` harness in `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py`
Scope-mode justification: The heal scope is fixed to `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, `.github/workflows/internal-clarify.yml`, `tests/**` and `changelog.d/*.md`, and Q1/Q2/Q3 = A all stay inside it. The complete version adds every needed gate and failure-path test. That is well within the "≤30 LOC more" rule, adds no dependency and no external interface, so it is chosen (§6: Correctness & safety ahead of Speed). The root-cause writer is under `scripts/`, so it is deferred to a follow-up issue as Q3 = A says, not dropped.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`
- `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py`
- `changelog.d/7516-clarify-label-missing-hold.md`

## Functions or modules to implement

**1. `clarify.yml` step "Resolve integration ref" (`id: refctx`)**

Mirror the `resolver_pr_not_open` block at lines 185-192:
- After the `resolver_pr_not_open` check, set `resolver_label_missing=true` only when all of these hold:
  - `resolver_rc` is 3;
  - `${resolver_err_file}` has a line matching `^::error::CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING issue=${issue_number} (pr=[0-9]+ )?outcome=refused reason=label_missing$`. This is anchored and names this issue only.
- In the stderr echo block, a `label_missing` match rewrites `::error::CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING ` to `::warning::CI_TRIAGE_PR_BRANCH_ROUTING `, the same way `pr_not_open` uses `::notice::`.
- Add a new `elif [ "${resolver_label_missing}" = "true" ]; then` branch. It must sit before the existing `elif [ "${resolver_rc}" -eq 3 ]; then` branch. `test_required_workflows_fail_closed_on_ci_triage_routing_refusal` slices from that branch to the fallback line and requires `exit 1` and no `GITHUB_OUTPUT` in that slice, so all new code, including any helper function, must stay before it.

The hold branch does these steps in order, using the step's existing `GH_TOKEN` (GH_PAT) and plain `gh api`, since support helpers are not staged yet:
1. Read the identity: `gh api user --jq .login`, validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9](-?[A-Za-z0-9])*$`. If that fails: `::error::INTEGRATION_REF_RESOLVE outcome=hold_failed reason=identity_unavailable issue=<n>` and `exit 1`.
2. Read the comments: `gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/${repo}/issues/${n}/comments?per_page=100"` piped to `jq --arg login --arg marker`. A marker counts only when the comment author is that login and the body, with trailing whitespace stripped, ends with `<!-- ai:integration-ref-label-missing:v1 issue=<n> -->`. A failed read or bad JSON gives `reason=comments_unavailable` and `exit 1`.
3. If no trusted marker exists, post one comment (`gh api -X POST .../issues/<n>/comments -f body=...`). A failed post gives `reason=comment_failed` and `exit 1`. The body is fixed text plus the issue number and run URL only, with no issue title or body text:
   - It explains that CI-triage routing was refused because the issue has the check-failure-triage markers but no `ai:check-triage` label. For an `ai:orchestrator-managed` issue it says the canonical `- Tracking issue (untrusted): #N` line is missing.
   - It gives the fix: restore `ai:check-triage` and remove `ai:orchestrator-managed`, or add the tracking line, then comment `/reclarify`.
   - `/reclarify` must appear only mid-sentence, never at the start of a line.
   - The comment's last line is the marker.
4. Add the label: `gh api -X POST .../issues/<n>/labels -f 'labels[]=ai:blocked'`. A failure gives `reason=label_failed` and `exit 1`. The label is added after the comment so the `ai:blocked` label event comes after the comment. That keeps `classify_unrouted_blocked_issues` (`scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:4108-4111`) from flagging it.
5. Write `label_missing_hold=true` and `ref=` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
6. Log `::warning::INTEGRATION_REF_RESOLVE outcome=held reason=label_missing issue=<n> comment=posted|present label=applied`, then `exit 0`.

Any other exit-3 reason still runs the existing `exit 1`.

**2. `clarify.yml`: gate every later step that runs on success**

Every step after `refctx` gets `steps.refctx.outputs.label_missing_hold != 'true'` in its `if:`:
- A step with no `if:` gets `if: steps.refctx.outputs.label_missing_hold != 'true'`. These are "Checkout repository", "Log checkout ref", "Configure git auth…", "Install Codex CLI", "Resolve workflow support ref", "Checkout workflow support source", "Ensure workflow support source checkout", "Stage workflow support files", "Create runtime workspace", "Fetch issue metadata", "Decide clarify route" and "Detect smoke test…".
- A step that already has an `if:` gets `steps.refctx.outputs.label_missing_hold != 'true' && (<existing>)`. This includes the `always()` steps "Semantic cache lookup" and "Write run summary". Gating "Decide clarify route" alone is not enough: when it is skipped, `skip_codex` is empty and `'' != 'true'` is true.
- Exempt, left unchanged:
  - steps whose condition needs `failure()` or `cancelled()`: "Record clarification run failed", "Comment on issue failure", "Queue failed reclarify for poller" and "Telegram failure notification". They never run on the successful hold path, and still run if the hold branch exits 1;
  - "Record GH_PAT budget at clarify end" and "Report refused AI engine fallbacks", which already guard themselves.
- The `heal-report` job is unchanged. `needs.clarify.result == 'failure'` is false on the hold path, so no heal report is filed.

**3. `clarify.yml`: Q2 guards for steps that run after the job stopped early**
- "Semantic cache lookup": if `${RUNTIME_DIR:-}` is empty or `scripts/semantic_cache.py` is missing, print `::warning::Semantic cache lookup skipped: runtime workspace or support scripts missing (job stopped before setup)`, write `cache_hit=false` and `exit 0`.
- "Write run summary": if `${RUNTIME_DIR:-}` is empty, print `::warning::` and `exit 0`. Use `${CODEX_OUTPUT_FILE:-}` in the file test.
- "Telegram failure notification": if `scripts/tg_helpers.sh` is missing, print `::warning::Telegram failure notification skipped: scripts/tg_helpers.sh not staged (job stopped before setup)` and `exit 0`. Use `${ISSUE_TITLE:-}`, because a failure between support staging and the issue-metadata fetch also hits `set -u`.
- This leaves the real refusal as the run's first `##[error]`, which feeds the failure headline and fingerprint.

**4. Follow-up issue (Q3 = A; out of this heal scope, do not edit here)**

The issue body and title of #7515 come from the close-and-reissue branch of `execute_stall_recovery_action`, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17144-17232`:
- `new_body` is `${orig_body}` copied verbatim at the top, then `---`, then `**⚠️ Re-issued from #N**`. The re-issue note is a suffix, so a truncated body excerpt shows only the triage header.
- `gh issue create` always adds `--label ai:clarification --label ai:orchestrator-managed`. It carries `ai:workflow-heal` (line 17222) but not `ai:check-triage`.
- It writes no `- Tracking issue (untrusted): #N` line unless `_stall_reissue_extra` is set.

That matches #7515's labels (`ai:clarification, ai:orchestrator-managed`) and #7511's shape.

Draft follow-up:
- Title: "Stall-recovery close_and_reissue copies triage markers into an ai:orchestrator-managed issue without ai:check-triage or a tracking line".
- Body:
  - cite these lines and #7511 / #7515;
  - fix: carry `ai:check-triage` when the source carries it (as `ai:workflow-heal` is carried), or, for a managed project child, append the standard `**Orchestrator metadata**` block with `- Tracking issue (untrusted): #<N>`;
  - check whether a standalone source should get `ai:orchestrator-managed` at all;
  - add a regression test that feeds the re-issued body and labels to `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh`;
  - add an `agents.d/` fragment documenting the clarify hold from this PR.
- `files_touched`: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`, `tests/test_resolve_integration_ref_ci_triage.py`, `tests/fixtures/integration_ref_resolver_ci_triage/*`, `agents.d/*`, `changelog.d/*`.

The implementer cannot create issues from the isolated container. It must copy this draft verbatim into the PR body under "Follow-up required (outside heal scope)" so it is filed when the PR lands.
